items.title: Trump blocked Netanyahu's planned Oct 10 multi-day Iran bombing campaign — FT (denied by JPost sources)
items.summary: Financial Times (Oct 21, three sources): Netanyahu ordered the IDF to prepare a multi-day bombing campaign for the weekend of Oct 10 — nuclear facilities, power plants, other civilian infrastructure and regime-linked sites, planned to be more intense than the Feb campaign — but Trump withheld approval over midterm concerns. Israel handed the US an updated target list incl. civilian infrastructure previously spared; unclear if US was to take part; one source says joint strikes in coming weeks 'not an unreasonable scenario'; another says the prep may have been partly a negotiating tactic ('Either there will be a deal or an attack'). WH spokesperson Anna Kelly reiterated the US will not strike Iran before Nov 3. Twist: Jerusalem Post sources told JBizNews the premise is wrong — the IDF was not ordered to prepare an Oct 10 strike in the way orders were handed down before prior conflicts, so 'Trump could not block an attack that was not planned'; narrative may serve Israeli-election optics (Israel votes Oct 27). Also reported in the same coverage: JPost sources said the Trump admin came 'very close' to approving a strike at least once in recent weeks; Ynet/Reuters: Tehran expects bombing to 'resume, sooner or later'.
